description: Probe-only rejection library for HIP_MLOPS_ENGINE Layernorm forward (runs on gfx950; the engine has no arch gate, HipMlopsEngine.cpp isApplicable asks each builder, LayernormPlanBuilder.cpp:76-172). Template: quick Layernorm/Variant2 (no saved statistics; add_tensors wires both mean (uid 5) and inv_variance (uid 6) for the families and samples that carry saved statistics). One feature per case, named by the `family` axis; every case is a graph the frontend accepts (LayerNormNode.hpp pre_validate: x rank >= 1, scale and bias same shape). Classes covered: unsupported attributes, mixed dtypes, int32/uint32 overflow, odd dims. Non-dense and padded strides are out of scope. The `expect` of a case is `declined` where the engine code shows it must decline (or, for a gap, where accepting means the kernel computes something else) and `declined_or_pass` where a correct engine may take the graph and the reference oracle can grade it; WRONG and CRASH always violate. The dtype families that may pass are restricted to the (x, scale/bias/stats, y) combinations the CPU and GPU references register (LayernormFpropSignatureKey.hpp getPlanBuilders), so an accepted case is graded, not UNEXERCISED. none: the control, pure float/half/bfloat16 with no saved statistics, ordinary rank 4 or 5, NCHW or NHWC, scale and bias covering the trailing axes from k; `declined_or_pass`. odd_dims: every dim of x not divisible by 4 (1, 2, primes, 127, 129, 255, 257); the engine has no divisibility gate (its kernels load one element at a time, DeclaredAlignment.hpp:15-23), so `declined_or_pass`. A graph with only one saved statistic (mean without inv_variance or the reverse) is rejected by the backend (LayernormOperationDescriptor::finalize), so it is not a probe. dt_scale_f: x and y half or bfloat16, scale, bias and statistics float: the plan builds separate x, y, scale/bias and statistic types (LayernormFwdPlan.cpp:123-142), registered reference combination: `declined_or_pass`. dt_y_f: x half or bfloat16 with y float (registered reference combination): `declined_or_pass`. dt_scale_bias: scale and bias differ in dtype: all affine tensors must share one dtype (LayernormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:152-158): `declined`. dt_mean_inv: mean and inv_variance differ in dtype: all statistic tensors must share one dtype (LayernormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:160-166): `declined`. dt_x_bad, dt_y_bad: x or y is int32, double or uint8; each io tensor must be float, half or bfloat16 (LayernormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:142-150): `declined`. dt_affine_bad (scale and bias) and dt_stat_bad (mean and inv_variance): the same dtypes outside the allowed sets (LayernormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:152-166): `declined`. rank_2, rank_3, rank_6: x of rank 2, 3 or 6 with the last axis normalized, packed row-major; the frontend accepts them, the engine takes rank 4 or 5 only (ApplicabilityChecks.cpp:31-41 validateDimensionCount, reached through LayernormApplicabilityChecks.cpp:117-135): `declined`. align: every device tensor declares the same alignment (1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes; powers of two only, because the backend rejects an execute whose pointer is not a multiple of the declared alignment, hip_kernel_provider_common/DeclaredAlignment.hpp:14-17); the engine declines a graph in which any non-virtual, non-pass-by-value tensor declares an alignment that is not a multiple of its element size (LayernormPlanBuilder.cpp:129-135, DeclaredAlignment.hpp:79-84, hip_kernel_provider_common/DeclaredAlignment.hpp:38-41): `declined` when the alignment is not a multiple of 2 or (not a multiple of 4 and some tensor is float), else `declined_or_pass`. ndc_mismatch [known gap]: normalized_dim_count one larger than the axes scale covers. The engine never reads normalized_dim_count (it derives the axes from scale and statistics, LayernormUtilities.cpp guessNormalizedDim; grep of hip_mlops_engine finds no use), the frontend does not check it for the forward node, and the CPU reference rejects the inconsistent graph (CpuFpReferenceLayernorm.hpp validateAffineShape): expected `declined`; an accept is a violation (a reference error or WRONG). overflow: `ovf` selects one size past a 32-bit limit, built at enforcement_level buildable (nothing is allocated, filled or executed): x_2_31 (2**31 elements) and x_2_32 (2**32 elements), inner_2_31 / inner_2_32 (one normalized row of 2**31 / 2**32 elements), outer_2_32 (2**32 rows). isApplicable has no overflow gate and LayernormFwdPlan.cpp:111-153 has no grid check at all; the kernels index with 32-bit unsigned constants (LayernormCommon.hpp:8-11, size_t x_idx = o * INNER_SIZE * STRIDE + ... at :35, unsigned multiplications) and the grid is cast to unsigned int (LayernormFwdPlan.cpp:151). All overflow cases are known gaps: `declined`; an accepted and built case is reported UNEXERCISED with the reason `accepted above the oracle ceiling`, a build exception is a CRASH finding. Not reachable from a space: compute_data_type, is_override_shape_enabled and ragged tensors (template literals; node_patches cannot reach node-level keys, tensor_patches set only alignment). Epsilon dtype is not probed (the template's epsilon carries a Float32Value). Known gaps are the families marked above; every other `declined` family is a stated unsupported configuration. The space is written for gfx950, the only device available; the engine runs there. It is probe-only: never frozen into a bundle. Axes (few on purpose, so the pairwise proof stays cheap): `family`; `shape` (ndim, n, c, d3, h, w, first normalized axis k, layout: 8 combinations covering rank 4 and 5, NCHW and NHWC and every split k); `odd` (n, c, d, h, w, none divisible by 4, read only by odd_dims); `x_dtype` (the base dtype of the pure families); `aux` (low-precision dtype, unsupported dtype, declared alignment, saved statistics, inv_rms dtype: 8 combinations, each family reads only the components it needs); `ovf` (the overflow variants).

derive.rank_r: 2 if family == 'rank_2' else (3 if family == 'rank_3' else 6)
derive.dd: (odd_d if is_odd else d3) if ndim == 5 else 1
derive.xs_h: ww if layout == 'nchw' else ww * cc
derive.xs_d: hh * ww if layout == 'nchw' else hh * ww * cc
derive.xs_c: dd * hh * ww if layout == 'nchw' else 1
derive.ps_h: pw if layout == 'nchw' else pw * pc
derive.ps_d: ph * pw if layout == 'nchw' else ph * pw * pc
derive.ps_c: pd * ph * pw if layout == 'nchw' else 1
derive.ss_h: sw if layout == 'nchw' else sw * sc
derive.ss_d: sh * sw if layout == 'nchw' else sh * sw * sc
derive.ss_c: sd * sh * sw if layout == 'nchw' else 1
derive.b_dims_x: [nn, cc, hh, ww] if ndim == 4 else [nn, cc, dd, hh, ww]
derive.b_dims_p: [1, pc, ph, pw] if ndim == 4 else [1, pc, pd, ph, pw]
derive.b_dims_s: [nn, sc, sh, sw] if ndim == 4 else [nn, sc, sd, sh, sw]
derive.b_str_x: [xs_n, xs_c, xs_h, xs_w] if ndim == 4 else [xs_n, xs_c, xs_d, xs_h, xs_w]
derive.b_str_p: [ps_n, ps_c, ps_h, ps_w] if ndim == 4 else [ps_n, ps_c, ps_d, ps_h, ps_w]
derive.b_str_s: [ss_n, ss_c, ss_h, ss_w] if ndim == 4 else [ss_n, ss_c, ss_d, ss_h, ss_w]
derive.r_dims_x: [nn, ww] if rank_r == 2 else ([nn, cc, ww] if rank_r == 3 else [nn, cc, dd, hh, 2, ww])
derive.r_dims_p: [1, ww] if rank_r == 2 else ([1, 1, ww] if rank_r == 3 else [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, ww])
derive.r_dims_s: [nn, 1] if rank_r == 2 else ([nn, cc, 1] if rank_r == 3 else [nn, cc, dd, hh, 2, 1])
derive.r_str_x: [ww, 1] if rank_r == 2 else ([cc * ww, ww, 1] if rank_r == 3 else [cc * dd * hh * 2 * ww, dd * hh * 2 * ww, hh * 2 * ww, 2 * ww, ww, 1])
derive.r_str_p: [ww, 1] if rank_r == 2 else ([ww, ww, 1] if rank_r == 3 else [ww, ww, ww, ww, ww, 1])
derive.r_str_s: [1, 1] if rank_r == 2 else ([cc, 1, 1] if rank_r == 3 else [cc * dd * hh * 2, dd * hh * 2, hh * 2, 2, 1, 1])
derive.ob: 2**32 if ovf == 'outer_2_32' else (1 if ovf in ['inner_2_31', 'inner_2_32'] else 2)
derive.ow: 2**15 if ovf in ['x_2_31', 'x_2_32'] else (2**31 if ovf == 'inner_2_31' else (2**32 if ovf == 'inner_2_32' else 4))
derive.dims_x: [ob, 1, oh, ow] if ov else (r_dims_x if rk else b_dims_x)
derive.dims_p: [1, 1, 1, ow] if ov else (r_dims_p if rk else b_dims_p)
derive.dims_s: [ob, 1, oh, 1] if ov else (r_dims_s if rk else b_dims_s)
derive.stride_x: [oh * ow, oh * ow, ow, 1] if ov else (r_str_x if rk else b_str_x)
derive.stride_p: [ow, ow, ow, 1] if ov else (r_str_p if rk else b_str_p)
derive.stride_s: [oh, oh, 1, 1] if ov else (r_str_s if rk else b_str_s)
derive.nd: 1 if (rk or ov) else ndim - k
derive.ty: 'float' if family == 'dt_y_f' else (bad_dt if family == 'dt_y_bad' else d0)
derive.tp: bad_dt if family == 'dt_affine_bad' else ('float' if mixed else d0)
derive.stats_both: family in ['dt_mean_inv', 'dt_stat_bad'] or (stats_ax == 'on' and family in ['none', 'odd_dims', 'dt_scale_f', 'dt_y_f', 'align', 'ndc_mismatch', 'overflow'])
derive.unc: family == 'align' and (al % 2 != 0 or (al % 4 != 0 and 'float' in ([tx, ty, tp, tb] + ([tm] if has_mean else []) + ([ti] if has_inv else []))))

expect: ${'declined_or_pass' if (family in ['none', 'odd_dims', 'dt_scale_f', 'dt_y_f'] or (family == 'align' and not unc)) else 'declined'}
